land.text: the Socialist Republic of Slovenia, one of the federation's republics; 'On 25 June 1991, Slovenia became independent'

predecessors.note: Plebiscite of 23 December 1990: 'more than 88% of the electorate voted for a sovereign and independent Slovenia'. Independence was suspended for three months by the Brioni Agreement of 7 July 1991.

correction.text: Slovenia in the year of its independence (25 June 1991): the same outline as Cliopatria's 1992 shape, only the years change

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts Slovenia in 1992 but the page dates independence to 25 June 1991. The Ten-Day War (27 June - 7 July) moved no border; the last Yugoslav soldiers left by 26 October 1991 (Ten-Day War page).

1992-2023, 19,575 km2 against the infobox 20,272 km2 (body text 20,271), ratio 0.97. The shape's 76 gazetteer cells equal Natural Earth's Slovenia (19,220 km2); the few cells it shares with Italy, Croatia and Hungary are outline noise at the border.
2024, identical to the 1992 shape. The page records no change of border after 1991 (EU 1 May 2004, NATO 2004, euro 1 January 2007); it does not mention the Piran Bay dispute with Croatia.

region.text: Slovenia within its republican borders: 'On 25 June 1991, Slovenia became independent'

ledger.note: 1991, 25 June: Slovenia declares independence from Yugoslavia. 'On 25 June 1991, Slovenia became independent.' Before it, 'On 23 December 1990, more than 88% of the electorate voted for a sovereign and independent Slovenia.' The page gives no boundary; the region is Cliopatria's 1992 shape, which matches the republic's border.

region.text: Slovenia and its border crossings, where the Yugoslav People's Army 'dispatched forces' in the early morning of 27 June

ledger.note: 1991, 27 June: the Ten-Day War begins. The page's infobox dates the war '27 June - 7 July 1991'; the first shot was fired 'on 26 June at 14:30 in Divaca'. The Slovenian page: 'the Yugoslav People's Army dispatched forces' on the early morning of 27 June.

1991, 7 July: the Brioni Accords end the fighting. The war lasted 'until 7 July 1991, when the Brioni Accords were signed': 'Slovenia and Croatia would postpone their independence for three months'; all Yugoslav units were to leave by the end of October, and the withdrawal 'was completed by 26 October'. Slovenian forces 'took control of all of the country's border crossings'.

wars.name: Ten-Day War

zones.text: the republic's territory and border crossings

wars.outcome: Slovenian victory: 'Slovenia gains full independence from Yugoslavia'; the Brioni Accords of 7 July 1991 suspended the declaration for three months and the Yugoslav army left by 26 October 1991.
wars.note: Infobox '27 June - 7 July 1991'; losses: JNA 45 killed, Slovenian forces 19 killed. The war moved no border, so the contest zone is the whole country.

certainty.note: The border is the former republican border of Yugoslavia and the Schengen/EU border of 2004-2007; the pages opened say nothing on the sea border with Croatia (Piran Bay), which is the one exception worth checking.

notes: Two pages opened (budget 1-2). Cliopatria's Slovenia shape is the republican border and needs no correction; the only addition is the 1991 start. The Slovenia page was silent on the Piran Bay / Drage / Sveta Gera disputes with Croatia and on the Treaty of Osimo with Italy, so no border event is recorded for them (a gap-filler could open 'Croatia-Slovenia border disputes'). The Ten-Day War page's summary of who held the border crossings on 27 June was not quoted: the extract was ambiguous about which side took them. The Slovenia page dates the last Yugoslav soldiers' departure only as 'the end of the month' after the 7 July entry, the Ten-Day War page as completed by 26 October 1991; the latter is used. No ruler list opened. All regions resolve in the gazetteer.
